docs.title: ASD-for-HRI
docs.text: asd4hri is a scalable Active Speaker Detection (ASD) for Human-Robot Interaction. For every video frame it detects the faces and classifies each of them as speaking or not speaking from the last frames of that face. It is built on the PAZ framework with Keras 3 and TensorFlow, and is evaluated on the UniTalk and AVA ActiveSpeaker datasets.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Everything is a chain of PAZ processors:

  1. ASD is the per-frame entry point. It detects the faces (YuNet by default, or RetinaFace or a Haar cascade), squares, clips and crops their boxes, and writes a class_name and a score into each box.
  2. ClassifyVVAD is the temporal part. It preprocesses every face (resizing for the image models, dlib landmarks for LipShape and FaceShape), buffers the last 38 frames of every face with BufferFeatures, runs the model every stride frames and averages the last predictions.

Until enough frames of a face are buffered, its box is labelled 'No Prediction yet' with a score of -1. Faces are identified by their position in the detection batch: there is no face tracking yet, the boxes are only sorted by position (FaceTracker).

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
The evaluation runs the ASD pipeline over the UniTalk or AVA ActiveSpeaker videos and scores the predictions against the ground truth.

Evaluation script runs inside the GPU Docker image, which runs Predictions and stats calculation. The individual steps can also be run on their own (see Individual steps below). All commands are issued from the repository root.

docs.title: 1. Predictions - Docker (GPU)
docs.text:
Build relative to the build context that is provided in the build command, in this case it is '.' (repository root) — the Dockerfile lives in docker/ but its COPY paths are relative:

docker build -f docker/Dockerfile_GPU --build-arg USER_UID=$(id -u) --build-arg USER_GID=$(id -g) \
    -t unitalk-gpu_buffer .

The container runs as a non-root user with the uid/gid given at build time, so the results it writes to the mounted data directory belong to you. Without the build args it uses 1000:1000. The mounted directory must be writable by that user.

docs.title: Full evaluation - src/experiments/run_evaluation.py
docs.text:
docker run -d --gpus all -v /Data/data:/app/data unitalk-gpu_buffer \
    --data_dir /app/data --no_download \
    --predictions_dir predictions_cnn1d_scores --architecture CNN2Plus1D
  • -v /Data/data:/app/data mounts the host data directory where the pipeline expects it.
  • Follow a detached run with docker logs -f <container>.

Everything after the image name is forwarded to the entrypoint (python -m src.experiments.run_evaluation) and replaces the image's default CMD, so repeat --data_dir. Prediction flags:

Flag Meaning --data_dir Root data directory, i.e. the mount point (default data) --dataset {unitalk,ava,wasd,easycom} Dataset to run over (default unitalk) --split Dataset split, UniTalk only (default val) --no_download Never fetch videos; skip the ones missing on disk --video <id> Run a single video only --predictions_dir Output folder, resolved relative to --data_dir (default predictions) --architecture Model to use (default CNN2Plus1D_Light) --stride Frames between predictions --boxes {detector,gt} Classify the detected faces (end-to-end, default) or the ground-truth face boxes (literature protocol); see Comparable metrics -v Also log INFO to the console

Stats flags:

Flag Meaning --groundtruth_csv Ground-truth CSV, relative to --data_dir (default csv/val_orig.csv for UniTalk, ava/annotations/ava_val_groundtruth.csv for AVA) --stats_dir Stats output folder, relative to --data_dir (default stats/<predictions_dir>) --iou_threshold Minimum IoU for a box match (default 0.5) --timestamp_tolerance_ms Max prediction/GT frame offset in ms (default 20) --workers Parallel scoring processes (default: all CPUs) --skip_stats Stop after predictions

Architectures: VVAD-LRS3-LSTM, CNN2Plus1D, CNN2Plus1D_Filters, CNN2Plus1D_Layers, CNN2Plus1D_Light, LipShape, FaceShape, LipShapeCausal, FaceShapeCausal.

LipShapeCausal / FaceShapeCausal (#45) predict every frame from that frame and the frames before it (zero look-ahead), from the first frame of a face on. --causal_mode streaming (default) keeps one LSTM state per face and costs one step per frame; --causal_mode window re-runs the model on the last --window frames (default 38). Retrain them with python -m src.model_training.train_causal_shape /Data/lipFeatures.h5 -f LipShape -o out/.

Audio-visual baselines (#40, #80; pip install -e '.[av]'): AV:LRX-ASD (0.50 M parameters), AV:LR-ASD (0.84 M), AV:Light-ASD (1.02 M) and AV:TalkNet (15.7 M), all with their AVA weights, and AV:FabuLight (1.02 M): FabuLight-ASD without body pose, the Light-ASD network trained on WASD. The networks come from pyasd, pinned to a commit; the weights are downloaded on first use into $ASD4HRI_WEIGHTS (default src/models, in the image /opt/asd4hri/weights) and checked by SHA-256. TalkNet uses the authors' original checkpoint, because pyasd's TalkNet file is a retrained model. They use the video's own audio track; every face is scored for its newest frame from the last --av_window frames (default 25) and the audio of the same span. Without audio, --audio_fallback noise (default) feeds low-level noise and visual uses the model's visual-only head; --no_audio forces the fallback.

UniTalk videos are downloaded from YouTube one at a time during the run; AVA videos are fetched all at once. The ground-truth CSV for either dataset is downloaded and built automatically if missing. With --no_download, nothing is downloaded and videos missing from --data_dir are skipped with a warning.

The run above writes to the host:

  • /Data/data/predictions_cnn1d_scores/: one <video_id>.csv per video plus aggregate_time.csv (frames processed and elapsed time).
  • /Data/data/stats/predictions_cnn1d_scores/: the stats output described below.
  • /Data/data/logs_stats/: stats log files.

docs.title: Benchmark: all models x datasets x protocols
docs.text:
python -m src.experiments.run_benchmark --data_dir /app/data --no_download --tag gpu \
    --architectures LipShapeCausal CNN2Plus1D_Light --datasets ava unitalk wasd easycom \
    --boxes gt detector [-- <extra run_evaluation flags>]

Every combination is one run_evaluation run into <data_dir>/benchmark/<tag>_<dataset>_<arch>_<boxes>/ (predictions + stats). Runs that already have a stats/summary.json are skipped, so an interrupted benchmark resumes, and --tag keeps cluster and Pi results apart. At the end all summaries are collected into benchmark/benchmark.csv and a booktabs benchmark/benchmark.tex. --dry_run prints the commands, --collect_only only rebuilds the table.

docs.title: WASD
docs.text: --dataset wasd evaluates on the WASD val split (Roxo et al.; 751 annotated 30-s sub-clips of 164 YouTube videos, CC-BY-SA-4.0). Without --no_download, the CSVs (0.3 GB) and the source videos (28.9 GB) are fetched with gdown from the official repository's Google Drive links into <data_dir>/wasd, and the sub-clips are cut exactly like WASD's own prepare_setup.py does. protocol_results.csv then also has one category:<code> row per WASD category: OC (optimal conditions), SI (speech impairment), FO (face occlusion), HVN (human voice noise) and SS (surveillance settings), taken from WASD's wasd_metadata.csv.

docs.title: EasyCom
docs.text: --dataset easycom --split test (sessions 10, 11; val = 4, 12) evaluates on EasyCom (Donley et al. 2021; AR glasses at a table, 20 fps, CC-BY-NC-4.0), the dataset closest to a stationary social robot. EasyCom has no official ASD protocol; easycom_dataset.py defines one: a face counts as speaking in the frames covered by that participant's speech transcription segments, and the face boxes become AVA-style rows (video_id = Session_<s>_<file>). The videos carry a participant-photo banner on the left; it is cropped away before detection and the boxes are converted to the cropped image. Download (~36 GB of the 70 GB release, only the needed folders) with the command in the module docstring into <data_dir>/easycom.

docs.title: Comparable metrics
docs.text:
Every run is scored with the official AVA script (src/eval/get_ava_active_speaker_performance.py) in the protocol that matches --boxes:

--boxes Protocol Comparable with gt The classifier runs on the ground-truth face tracks; the detector is skipped. mAP over all GT boxes. The mAP that AVA / UniTalk / WASD papers report detector End-to-end mAP@0.5: detections are matched one-to-one to GT boxes at IoU ≥ 0.5; detections without a GT box count as false positives. Ego4D's mAP@0.5; the whole pipeline (detector + tracking + classifier)

In both protocols, a GT box without a score (missed by the detector, or no prediction yet while a buffer fills) gets score 0, because the official script needs a score for every GT box.

<stats_dir>/protocol_results.csv has one row per video and a pooled row (all GT boxes of the run ranked together, as papers report it):

Column Meaning map Official AVA mAP in the run's protocol auc Area under the ROC curve precision, recall, f1, balanced_accuracy, tp/fp/fn/tn At the decision threshold 0.5 coverage Share of GT boxes that got a score det_recall, dropped_faces, det_precision Face detector: share of GT faces found at IoU ≥ 0.5, number missed, share of detections that are GT faces (detector runs only) n_<bin>, map_<bin>, det_recall_<bin> The same per face width: small < 64 px, medium 64–128 px, large > 128 px

summary.json holds the pooled numbers together with the run configuration (dataset, architecture, boxes, stride, host, CPU architecture, git commit) and the speed. For gt runs, ava_groundtruth.csv and ava_predictions.csv can be re-scored with the official script itself:

python src/eval/get_ava_active_speaker_performance.py \
    -g stats/<run>/ava_groundtruth.csv -p stats/<run>/ava_predictions.csv

docs.title: Where the time goes
docs.text:
ASD records the time of every pipeline stage (switch off with ASD(profile=False)):

Stage What it covers read Decoding the next video frame detect, track Face detector, ordering/tracking of the boxes crop Squaring, clipping and cropping the faces preprocess Resize (image models) or dlib landmarks (*Shape models) buffer, normalize Per-face temporal buffers, landmark normalisation model The classifier's forward pass, including the GPU sync average Smoothing the scores over the last predictions audio_decode, audio Audio-visual models: decoding the track, MFCCs per window frame Everything per frame, from detect to average

Per video, <predictions_dir>/timing/<video_id>.csv has calls, total, mean/median/p95/max ms and ms per face for each stage. Over the run, <stats_dir>/stage_times.csv gives ms per frame and the share of the frame time, and summary.json has stage_ms_per_frame.

aggregate_results.csv keeps the older metrics (threshold metrics and AP over matched boxes only) for comparison with earlier runs.

docs.text: The prediction and the stats phase can also be run on their own, and the stats phase can run outside the Docker image. Both, and the files the stats phase writes, are described in the README.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
asd4hri needs Python 3.10 or newer. dlib is compiled from source during the installation, so CMake and a C++ compiler must be available (e.g. apt install build-essential cmake).

git clone https://github.com/adriandavidauer/ASD-for-HRI.git
cd ASD-for-HRI
pip install -e .            # the library
pip install -e '.[dev]'     # plus tests, linters and the experiment dependencies
pip install -e '.[docs]'    # plus the tools to build this documentation

On x86_64 the GPU build of ONNX Runtime is installed; it falls back to the CPU when no GPU is available. The model weights are downloaded on first use. To download all of them at once, run python src/initialize_models.py.

For development there is a devcontainer based on docker/Dockerfile_GPU; see the README.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
ASD processes one frame per call and returns the image and the face boxes with their predictions:

import cv2
from asd4hri.asd import ASD

pipeline = ASD(architecture='CNN2Plus1D_Light')
video = cv2.VideoCapture('video.mp4')
while True:
    ok, frame = video.read()
    if not ok:
        break
    for box in pipeline(frame)['boxes2D']:
        print(box.coordinates, box.class_name, box.score)

The architectures are listed in Architecture_Options: VVAD-LRS3-LSTM, CNN2Plus1D, CNN2Plus1D_Filters, CNN2Plus1D_Layers, CNN2Plus1D_Light, LipShape and FaceShape. stride sets how often the model runs, averaging_window_size and weighted how the last predictions are smoothed; see the API reference for all options.

To run it live on a camera with PAZ:

from paz.backend.camera import Camera, VideoPlayer
from asd4hri.asd import ASD

pipeline = ASD(architecture='LipShape', annotate_output=True)
player = VideoPlayer((640, 480), pipeline, Camera(0))
player.run()

docs.title: ClassifyVVAD(architecture='CNN2Plus1D_Light', stride=38, averaging_window_size=2, weighted=False, max_consecutive_empty=5, timer=None, causal_mode='streaming', window_size=38)
docs.text:
Bases: Processor

Visual Voice Activity Detection pipeline for cropped face video clips.

Classifies speaking vs. not speaking. Expects a batch of face images per call, each image representing a different entity. Entities are identified either by their position in the batch (the order must then be stable across calls) or by the optional ids. Images, or the shape features extracted from them, are buffered until a full sample for the model is collected. Returns a batch of (averaged) predictions, each corresponding to the entity at the same index of the input batch, or None where no prediction is available yet.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default architecture

Name of the architecture to use. One of Architecture_Options: 'VVAD-LRS3-LSTM', 'CNN2Plus1D', 'CNN2Plus1D_Filters', 'CNN2Plus1D_Layers', 'CNN2Plus1D_Light', 'LipShape' or 'FaceShape'.

'CNN2Plus1D_Light' stride

Number of frames between two predictions. A low stride is computationally expensive (high update rate), a high stride adds latency (low update rate).

38 averaging_window_size

Number of consecutive predictions that are averaged. Set to 1 to disable averaging.

2 weighted

If True, the predictions in the averaging window are weighted by their position (index + 1), so newer predictions count more. If False, a plain average is used.

False max_consecutive_empty

Number of consecutive missing face images after which the buffer of an entity is cleared.

5

Load the classifier and assemble the preprocessing, buffering and averaging steps.

timer is an optional StageTimer that records the time of every step (#76). Asserts that architecture is in Architecture_Options.

Source code in src/asd4hri/asd.py 
def __init__(self, architecture='CNN2Plus1D_Light',
             stride=38, averaging_window_size=2, weighted=False, max_consecutive_empty=5,
             timer=None, causal_mode='streaming', window_size=38):
    """Load the classifier and assemble the preprocessing, buffering and averaging steps.

    ``timer`` is an optional ``StageTimer`` that records the time of every step (#76).
    Asserts that ``architecture`` is in ``Architecture_Options``.
    """
    super(ClassifyVVAD, self).__init__()
    self.timer = timer or NULL_TIMER
    assert architecture in Architecture_Options, f"'{architecture}' is not in {Architecture_Options}"
    assert causal_mode in Causal_Modes, f"'{causal_mode}' is not in {Causal_Modes}"

    self.classifier, input_size = load_vvad_classifier(architecture)
    self.causal = architecture in Causal_Architectures
    self.causal_mode = causal_mode
    if self.causal:
        # one prediction per frame: the stride and the fixed sample length don't apply
        input_size = (window_size,) + tuple(input_size[1:])
        stride = 1
        self.stream = StreamingFeatureLSTM(self.classifier) if causal_mode == 'streaming' else None
        # compiled once for any batch size and length; eager Keras calls cost ~20 ms each
        num_landmarks = input_size[1]
        self._window_fn = tf.function(
            lambda x: self.classifier(x, training=False),
            input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None, None, num_landmarks, 2], tf.float32)])
        self.missed = {}
        self.max_consecutive_empty = max_consecutive_empty
    # Dummy predict to fully initialize
    self.classifier(np.zeros((1,) + tuple(input_size)))

    self.class_names = get_class_names('VVAD_LRS3')
    self.is_shape = 'Shape' in architecture

    # works on a batch of face images, not on a batch of samples, so it runs before buffering
    if self.is_shape:
        self.preprocess = GetShapeFeatures(architecture=architecture.replace('Causal', ''))
    else:
        # not normalized to [0, 1] because the model is trained on images in [0, 255]
        self.preprocess = PreprocessImages(input_size[1:3], normalize=False)
    # buffers the incoming face images or features into samples; a causal model in 'window'
    # mode predicts from whatever is buffered so far (1..window_size frames)
    self.buffer_features = BufferFeatures(input_size, stride=stride, max_consecutive_empty=max_consecutive_empty,
                                          return_incomplete_samples=self.causal)
    self.normalize = NormalizeShapeSample() if self.is_shape and not self.causal else None
    self.predict = PredictWithNones(model=self.classifier, postprocess=flatten_predictions)

    # Buffer predictions with stride 1 and return_incomplete_samples, so that something is
    # returned on every call. max_consecutive_empty = stride, so that a model giving no
    # prediction for stride steps does not reset the buffer.
    self.buffer_predictions = BufferFeatures((averaging_window_size,), stride=1, max_consecutive_empty=stride, return_incomplete_samples=True)
    # normalize to [0, 1] so that the output is in [0, 1] independent of averaging_window_size
    self.avg = AveragePredictions(weighted=weighted, normalize=True)

def call(self, images, ids=None):
    """Classify a batch of face images, one per entity.

    Args:
        images: Batch of cropped RGB face images.
        ids: Optional entity ids, one per image. If given, each entity keeps its own
            temporal buffer regardless of its position in the batch.

    Returns:
        list: One (averaged) score in [0, 1] per image, or None where no prediction is
        available yet.
    """
    timer, n = self.timer, len(images)
    with timer.stage('preprocess', n):
        features = self.preprocess(images)
    if self.causal:
        return self._call_causal(features, ids)
    with timer.stage('buffer', n):
        samples = self.buffer_features(features, ids)
    n_samples = sum(sample is not None for sample in samples)
    if self.normalize is not None:
        with timer.stage('normalize', n_samples):
            samples = self.normalize(samples)
    if n_samples:
        with timer.stage('model', n_samples):
            predictions = self.predict(samples)
    else:
        predictions = None
    if predictions is None or len(predictions) == 0:
        predictions = [None] * n
    with timer.stage('average', n):
        return self.avg(self.buffer_predictions(list(predictions), ids))

def reset(self):
    """Clear the temporal state: the feature buffers and the prediction averaging window."""
    self.buffer_features.reset()
    self.buffer_predictions.reset()
    if self.causal and self.stream is not None:
        self.stream.reset()
        self.missed = {}

docs.text:
Bases: Processor

Active Speaker Detection pipeline.

Detects faces in each RGB frame, crops them and classifies every face as speaking or not speaking with ClassifyVVAD. Multiple consecutive frames are needed before the first prediction is produced; until then boxes are labelled 'No Prediction yet' with score -1.

Example 
pipeline = ASD(architecture='LipShape')
camera = Camera(0)
player = VideoPlayer((640, 480), pipeline, camera)
player.run()

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default architecture

Name of the architecture to use. One of Architecture_Options: 'VVAD-LRS3-LSTM', 'CNN2Plus1D', 'CNN2Plus1D_Filters', 'CNN2Plus1D_Layers', 'CNN2Plus1D_Light', 'LipShape' or 'FaceShape'.

'CNN2Plus1D_Light' stride

Number of frames between two predictions. A low stride is computationally expensive, a high stride adds latency.

2 averaging_window_size

Number of consecutive predictions that are averaged. Set to 1 to disable averaging.

3 decision_threshold

Score above which a face is classified as speaking.

0.5 weighted

If True, the averaging window is weighted by the position of each prediction, so newer predictions count more.

True max_consecutive_empty

Number of frames a face may be missing before its buffer is cleared. A low number can cause short samples or missing predictions for models with a fixed sample length; a high number can cause glitches in samples.

2 annotate_output

If True, the bounding box, score and predicted label are drawn on the returned image.

False detector

Face detector to use. One of FaceDetector_Options. Only 'YuNet', 'HaarCascade' and 'RetinaFace' are implemented.

'YuNet' input_size

(width, height) of the input images, used by the YuNet detector. If None, it is set at runtime, which can slow the pipeline down slightly.

None face_tracking_approach

How faces are kept in a stable order across frames. One of FaceTracking_Options; see FaceTracker.

'sort' profile

If True, the time of every stage is recorded in self.timer (a StageTimer); see #76.

True av_window

Frames per prediction for the audio-visual architectures ('AV:'). 25 audio_fallback

What the audio-visual models get without audio: 'noise' or 'visual' (visual-only back end); see asd4hri.av.AVClassifier.

'noise' causal_mode

Only for the causal architectures (Causal_Architectures): 'streaming' keeps one LSTM state per face and costs one step per frame, 'window' re-runs the model on the last window_size frames. Both predict every frame with zero look-ahead (#45).

'streaming' window_size

Frames per prediction in the causal 'window' mode.

38

Build the face detection, cropping and classification steps.

Raises:

Type Description NotImplementedError

If detector is 'InsightFace' or 'YOLOv10-Face'.

ValueError

If detector is unknown.

def __init__(self, architecture='CNN2Plus1D_Light', stride=2, averaging_window_size=3, decision_threshold=0.5,
             weighted= True, max_consecutive_empty=2, annotate_output=False, detector='YuNet', input_size=None, face_tracking_approach='sort',
             profile=True, causal_mode='streaming', window_size=38, av_window=25,
             audio_fallback='noise'):
    """Build the face detection, cropping and classification steps.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: If ``detector`` is 'InsightFace' or 'YOLOv10-Face'.
        ValueError: If ``detector`` is unknown.
    """
    super(ASD, self).__init__()
    self.timer = StageTimer(enabled=profile)
    self.av = None
    self.annotate_output = annotate_output
    self.offsets = [0,0]
    self.colors = [[0, 255, 0], [255, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0]]
    self.absent_counts = []
    self.face_tracking_approach = face_tracking_approach
    if self.face_tracking_approach not in FaceTracking_Options:
        raise ValueError(f"Face tracking approach must be one of {FaceTracking_Options} but is {self.face_tracking_approach}")
    self.face_tracker = FaceTracker(approach=self.face_tracking_approach)
    #detection
    self.copy = pr.Copy()
    if detector == 'HaarCascade':
        self.detect = dt.HaarCascadeFrontalFace()
    elif detector == 'YuNet':
        self.detect = FaceDetectorYN(input_size=input_size) # TODO: parameter forwarding with kwargs?
    elif detector == 'RetinaFace':
        self.detect = FaceDetectorRetinaFace() # TODO: parameter forwarding with kwargs?
    elif detector ==  'InsightFace':
        raise NotImplementedError
    elif detector == 'YOLOv10-Face':
        raise NotImplementedError
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown detector {detector}. Must be one of {FaceDetector_Options}")
    self.square = SequentialProcessor()
    self.square.add(pr.SquareBoxes2D())
    self.square.add(pr.OffsetBoxes2D(self.offsets))
    self.clip = pr.ClipBoxes2D()
    self.crop = pr.CropBoxes2D()


    self.vvad_args = dict(
        stride=stride,
        averaging_window_size=averaging_window_size,
        weighted=weighted,
        architecture=architecture, max_consecutive_empty=max_consecutive_empty,
        timer=self.timer, causal_mode=causal_mode, window_size=window_size
    )
    self.class_names = list(get_class_names('VVAD_LRS3'))
    corrected_class_names = [self.class_names[1], self.class_names[0]] # in PAZ the order is speaking, not-speaking but we need it the other way around.
    self.decision_threshold = decision_threshold
    self.corrected_class_names = corrected_class_names
    if architecture.startswith(AV_PREFIX):
        # audio-visual model (#40, #80): crops its own faces from the frame, needs set_audio()
        self.av = AVClassifier(architecture[len(AV_PREFIX):], window=av_window,
                               stride=stride, max_consecutive_empty=max_consecutive_empty,
                               audio_fallback=audio_fallback, timer=self.timer)
        self.classifier = None
    else:
        self.classifier = AddClassAndScoreToBoxes(ClassifyVVAD(**self.vvad_args), class_names=corrected_class_names, decision_threshold=decision_threshold)


    self.class_names.append('No Prediction yet')

    self.draw = pr.DrawBoxes2D(self.class_names, self.colors, True)
    self.wrap = pr.WrapOutput(['image', 'boxes2D'])

def call(self, image, boxes2D=None, ids=None, timestamp=None):
    """Detect faces in one frame and classify each of them as speaking or not speaking.

    Args:
        image: RGB image as a numpy array of shape ``(height, width, 3)``.
        boxes2D: Optional face boxes (``paz.abstract.messages.Box2D`` in pixels). If given,
            the face detector and tracker are skipped and these boxes are classified,
            e.g. the ground-truth boxes of a dataset (#75).
        ids: Optional entity ids, one per box in ``boxes2D``. Each id keeps its own temporal
            buffer. Without ids, faces are identified by their (tracked) position.
        timestamp: Time of the frame in seconds; the audio-visual models need it to cut the
            matching audio.

    Returns:
        dict: ``{'image': image, 'boxes2D': boxes2D}``. ``boxes2D`` is a list of
        ``paz.abstract.messages.Box2D`` whose ``class_name`` and ``score`` hold the prediction.
        The image has the boxes drawn on it if ``annotate_output`` is True.
    """
    timer = self.timer
    with timer.stage('frame'):
        if boxes2D is None:
            # get the face boxes and crop the faces from the image
            with timer.stage('detect'):
                image_copy = self.copy(image)
                boxes2D = self.detect(image_copy)['boxes2D']
            with timer.stage('track', len(boxes2D)):
                boxes2D = self.face_tracker(boxes2D)
            ids = None
        n = len(boxes2D)
        if self.av is not None:
            # TalkNet-style models crop the (unsquared) box themselves
            with timer.stage('crop', n):
                boxes2D = self.clip(image, boxes2D)
            scores = self.av(image, [b.coordinates for b in boxes2D], ids, timestamp)
            for score, box in zip(scores, boxes2D):
                if score is None:
                    box.score, box.class_name = -1.0, 'No Prediction yet'
                else:
                    box.score = float(score)
                    box.class_name = self.corrected_class_names[int(score > self.decision_threshold)]
        else:
            with timer.stage('crop', n):
                boxes2D = self.square(boxes2D)
                boxes2D = self.clip(image, boxes2D)
                cropped_images = self.crop(image, boxes2D)

            # call classifyVVAD for the whole batch of faces; it times its own steps
            boxes2D = self.classifier(cropped_images, boxes2D, ids)

        # only if flag is set
        if self.annotate_output:
            with timer.stage('annotate', n):
                image = self.draw(image, boxes2D)
        return self.wrap(image, boxes2D)

def load_vvad_classifier(architecture):
    """Load the Keras classifier model for the given architecture.

    The ``LipShape`` and ``FaceShape`` weights are downloaded to ``src/models`` on first use.

    Args:
        architecture: Name of the architecture to load. One of ``Architecture_Options``:
            'VVAD-LRS3-LSTM', 'CNN2Plus1D', 'CNN2Plus1D_Filters', 'CNN2Plus1D_Layers',
            'CNN2Plus1D_Light', 'LipShape' or 'FaceShape'.

        shape of one sample expected by the model, e.g. ``(38, 96, 96, 3)`` for the image models,
        ``(38, 20, 2)`` for 'LipShape' and ``(38, 68, 2)`` for 'FaceShape'.

    if architecture == 'VVAD-LRS3-LSTM':
        return (VVAD_LRS3_LSTM(weights='VVAD_LRS3'), (38, 96, 96, 3))
    elif architecture.startswith('CNN2Plus1D'):
        return (CNN2Plus1D(weights='VVAD_LRS3', architecture=str(architecture)), (38, 96, 96, 3))
    elif architecture in Causal_Architectures:

        get_file(filename, URL + filename, cache_subdir=str(Path(__file__).absolute().parent.parent / "models" ))
        num_landmarks = 20 if architecture.startswith('Lip') else 68
        return (load_model(str(Path(__file__).absolute().parent.parent / "models" / filename)), (None, num_landmarks, 2))
    elif architecture == 'LipShape':
        filename = 'paz_LipShape_0.8958.keras'
        get_file(filename, URL + filename, cache_subdir=str(Path(__file__).absolute().parent.parent / "models" ))
        return (load_model(str(Path(__file__).absolute().parent.parent / "models" / 'paz_LipShape_0.8958.keras')), (38, 20, 2))
    elif architecture == 'FaceShape':

        return (load_model(str(Path(__file__).absolute().parent.parent / "models" / 'faceFeatureModel.keras')), (38, 68, 2))

def __init__(self, model):
    """Copy the weights out of the Keras model."""
    import numpy as np
    lstm = model.get_layer('lstm')
    self.kernel, self.recurrent, self.bias = (np.asarray(w) for w in lstm.get_weights())
    self.units = self.recurrent.shape[0]
    gamma, beta, mean, var = model.get_layer('bn').get_weights()
    eps = model.get_layer('bn').epsilon
    self.bn_scale = gamma / np.sqrt(var + eps)
    self.bn_shift = beta - mean * self.bn_scale
    self.w1, self.b1 = model.get_layer('dense').get_weights()
    self.w2, self.b2 = model.get_layer('out').get_weights()
    self.states = {}

def step(self, frames, ids):
    """Advance the given entities by one frame.

    Args:
        frames: Array ``(n, num_landmarks, 2)`` of normalized landmarks, one per entity.
        ids: Entity ids, one per frame.

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: ``(n,)`` speaking probabilities for these frames.
    """
    import numpy as np
    x = np.asarray(frames, dtype=np.float32).reshape(len(ids), -1)
    u = self.units
    h = np.stack([self.states.get(i, (np.zeros(u, np.float32),) * 2)[0] for i in ids])
    c = np.stack([self.states.get(i, (np.zeros(u, np.float32),) * 2)[1] for i in ids])
    z = x @ self.kernel + h @ self.recurrent + self.bias      # Keras gate order: i, f, c, o
    i_g = self._sigmoid(z[:, :u])
    f_g = self._sigmoid(z[:, u:2 * u])
    c = f_g * c + i_g * np.tanh(z[:, 2 * u:3 * u])
    h = self._sigmoid(z[:, 3 * u:]) * np.tanh(c)
    for k, key in enumerate(ids):
        self.states[key] = (h[k], c[k])
    y = np.maximum(0.0, (h * self.bn_scale + self.bn_shift) @ self.w1 + self.b1)
    return self._sigmoid(y @ self.w2 + self.b2).reshape(-1)

def buildCausalFeatureLSTM(num_landmarks, lstm_dims=32, dense_dims=512, **kwargs):
    """Build the causal (per-frame) landmark LSTM for variable-length input (#45).

    Same layers and size as ``buildFeatureLSTM`` with one LSTM and one dense layer, but the LSTM
    returns its output at every time step and the dense layers are applied per step. The output
    at frame *t* therefore uses only frames 0..t (zero look-ahead), and the input can have any
    length, from a single frame upwards.

    Args:
        num_landmarks: Number of landmarks per frame (20 for lips, 68 for the whole face).
        lstm_dims: Number of LSTM units.
        dense_dims: Number of units of the ReLU dense layer.
        **kwargs: Ignored.

    Returns:
        keras.Model: Input ``(batch, time, num_landmarks, 2)``, output ``(batch, time, 1)``
        speaking probabilities. Compiled with Adam and binary cross-entropy.
    """
    import keras
    from keras import layers

    inputs = keras.Input(shape=(None, num_landmarks, 2))
    x = layers.Reshape((-1, num_landmarks * 2))(inputs)
    x = layers.LSTM(lstm_dims, return_sequences=True, name='lstm')(x)
    x = layers.BatchNormalization(name='bn')(x)
    x = layers.Dense(dense_dims, activation='relu', name='dense')(x)
    outputs = layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid', name='out')(x)
    model = keras.Model(inputs, outputs, name=f'CausalFeatureLSTM_{num_landmarks}')
    model.compile(loss='binary_crossentropy', optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(1e-3),
                  metrics=['accuracy'])
    return model

def normalize_shape_frames(landmarks):
    """Normalize landmarks frame by frame, using no information from other frames (#45).

    Each frame is centred on the mean of its landmarks and scaled by its largest absolute
    coordinate, so it lies in [-1, 1]. Unlike ``NormalizeShapeSample``, which uses the first
    frame and the maximum over the whole sample, this is causal and independent of the length.

    Args:
        landmarks: Array of shape ``(..., num_landmarks, 2)``.

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: Float32 array of the same shape.
    """
    import numpy as np
    x = np.asarray(landmarks, dtype=np.float32)
    x = x - x.mean(axis=-2, keepdims=True)
    scale = np.abs(x).max(axis=(-2, -1), keepdims=True)
    return x / np.maximum(scale, 1e-6)

def __init__(self, input_size, stride=25, max_consecutive_empty=5, return_incomplete_samples=False):
    """Set up the buffer configuration and empty internal buffers.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``input_size[0]`` is smaller than ``stride``.
    """
    self.buffer_size = input_size[0]
    if self.buffer_size < stride:
        raise ValueError('Buffer size must be equal or larger than stride')
    super(BufferFeatures, self).__init__()
    self.stride = stride 
    self.max_consecutive_empty = max_consecutive_empty
    self.return_incomplete_samples = return_incomplete_samples
    # Buffers: 
    self.buffers = []
    # Counters for return after stride
    self.timesteps_since_last_return = [] # I have to keep track of that for each internal buffer, because otherwise a full buffer could return even if only input for another buffer came in.
    self.missed_consecutive_timesteps = []

def call(self, batch_of_features, ids=None):
    """Add one batch of features to the internal buffers.

    Args:
        batch_of_features: Sorted list-like object of features with shape
            ``(N, dim0, dim1, ...)`` where N is the batch size. Entries may be None.
        ids: Optional entity ids, one per feature. If given, every entity gets its own
            buffer keyed by its id, independent of its position in the batch; entities
            missing from a call count as empty for that call. If None, buffers are matched
            by batch position.

    Returns:
        list: One entry per input position: the corresponding buffer (a ``collections.deque``
        holding up to ``timesteps`` features) if it is ready to be returned, otherwise None.
    """
    if ids is not None:
        return self._call_keyed(batch_of_features, ids)
    batch_return = []
    for i, features in enumerate(batch_of_features):
        if i == len(self.buffers):
            self.buffers.append(deque(maxlen=self.buffer_size))
            self.timesteps_since_last_return.append(0)
            self.missed_consecutive_timesteps.append(0)
        if features is None:
            self.missed_consecutive_timesteps[i] += 1
        else:
            self.buffers[i].append(features)
            self.missed_consecutive_timesteps[i] = 0
        self.timesteps_since_last_return[i] += 1 
        if (self.return_incomplete_samples) or (len(self.buffers[i]) == self.buffer_size and self.timesteps_since_last_return[i] >= self.stride):
            batch_return.append(self.buffers[i])
            self.timesteps_since_last_return[i] = 0
        else:
            batch_return.append(None) # necessary to keep ordering
        # resetting
        if self.missed_consecutive_timesteps[i] >= self.max_consecutive_empty:
            self.reset(index=i)
    # update missed_consecutive_timesteps for buffers in the end of the list if input list is shorter than self.buffers
    # need to go backwards to pop
    for j in range(len(self.buffers) - 1, len(batch_of_features) - 1, -1):
        self.missed_consecutive_timesteps[j] += 1
        if self.missed_consecutive_timesteps[j] >= self.max_consecutive_empty:
            if j == len(self.buffers) - 1:
                # remove dangeling
                self.buffers.pop()
                self.timesteps_since_last_return.pop()
                self.missed_consecutive_timesteps.pop()
            else:
                # a later buffer is still alive, so this one keeps its index
                self.reset(index=j)
    return batch_return

def reset(self, index=None):

def call(self, face_images):

    ret_batch = []

def call(self, batch_of_list_of_values):
    """Average every list of values in the batch.

    Args:
        batch_of_list_of_values: Batch of lists of values. Entries may be None or empty.

    Returns:
        list: One averaged value per entry, None for None or empty entries. Returns None if the
        batch is None and an empty list if the batch is empty.
    """
    if batch_of_list_of_values is None:
        return None
    if len(batch_of_list_of_values) == 0:
        return []
    else:
        # create mapping and remove Nones and empty lists from the batch
        non_none_pairs = [(i, val) for i, val in enumerate(batch_of_list_of_values) if val is not None and len(val) != 0]  
        if not non_none_pairs:
            return [None] * len(batch_of_list_of_values)
        indices, non_nones = zip(*non_none_pairs)    

        # Get sample lengths and dimensions
        lengths = np.array([len(x) for x in non_nones])
        max_len = lengths.max()
        # Build a padded 2D matrix filled with zeros
        padded = np.zeros((len(non_nones), max_len))
        for i, buffer in enumerate(non_nones):
            padded[i, :len(buffer)] = buffer
        if self.weighted:
            # Create index weights: [1, 2, 3] and multiply
            weights = np.arange(1, max_len+1)
            padded = padded * weights
        # Sum across rows and divide by the REAL original length of each sample
        mean = np.array(padded).sum(axis=1) / lengths

        # normalize eachto [0, 1] if desired
        if self.normalize:
            max_vals = np.array([np.sum(np.arange(1, x+1))/x for x in lengths])
            mean = mean / max_vals
        # apply mapping to recreate batch with Nones
        ret_batch = [None] * len(batch_of_list_of_values)
        for idx, val in zip(indices, mean):
            ret_batch[idx] = val
        return ret_batch

def call(self, cropped_images, boxes, ids=None):
    """Classify the cropped images and update the boxes in place.

    Boxes without a score get the class name 'No Prediction yet' and a score of -1.0.

    Args:
        cropped_images: Batch of cropped images, one per box.

        ids: Optional entity ids, one per box, passed on to the classifier.

    scores = self.classify(cropped_images) if ids is None else self.classify(cropped_images, ids)
    for score, box2D in zip(scores, boxes):
        if score is None:
            class_name = 'No Prediction yet'
            score = -1.0
        else:
            class_name = self.class_name[1] if score > self.decision_threshold else self.class_name[0]
        box2D.score = score
        box2D.class_name = class_name
        # return_boxes.append(add_class_and_score({'class_name': class_name, 'scores': [score]}, box2D))

    return {'image': image, 'boxes2D': boxes2D}

def call(self, image):
    """Detect faces in an image.

    Args:
        image: Image as a numpy array of shape ``(height, width, 3)``.

    Returns:
        dict: ``{'image': image, 'boxes2D': boxes2D}`` where ``boxes2D`` is a list of
        ``paz.abstract.messages.Box2D`` in pixel coordinates with the detection score and the
        class name 'Face'. The image has the boxes drawn on it if ``draw`` is True.
    """
    orig_height, orig_width, _ = image.shape

    # RGB in (as everywhere in the ASD pipeline); the model expects BGR with BGR means (#77)
    img = cv2.resize(cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR), (640, 640)).astype(np.float32)
    im_height, im_width, _ = img.shape
    # scale = np.array([img.shape[1], img.shape[0], img.shape[1], img.shape[0]])
    img -= (104, 117, 123)
    img = img.transpose(2, 0, 1)
    img = np.expand_dims(img, axis=0)

    # tic = time.time()
    inputs = {"input": img}
    loc, conf, _ = self.retinaface.run(None, inputs)
    # print('net forward time: {:.4f}s'.format(time.time() - tic))

    # tic = time.time()
    priorbox = PriorBox(cfg, image_size=(im_height, im_width), format="numpy")
    priors = priorbox.forward()

    prior_data = priors

    boxes = decode(np.squeeze(loc, axis=0), prior_data, cfg['variance'])
    # rescale the boxes to original image size
    boxes = boxes * np.array([orig_width, orig_height, orig_width, orig_height])
    scores = np.squeeze(conf, axis=0)[:, 1]

    # landms = decode_landm(np.squeeze(landms.data, axis=0), prior_data, cfg['variance'])

    # scale1 = np.array([img.shape[3], img.shape[2], img.shape[3], img.shape[2],
    #                        img.shape[3], img.shape[2], img.shape[3], img.shape[2],
    #                        img.shape[3], img.shape[2]])
    # landms = landms * scale1 / resize

    # ignore low scores
    inds = np.where(scores > self.conf_threshold)[0]
    boxes = boxes[inds]
    # landms = landms[inds]
    scores = scores[inds]

    # keep top-K before NMS
    order = scores.argsort()[::-1][:self.pre_nms_top_k]
    boxes = boxes[order]
    # landms = landms[order]
    scores = scores[order]

    # do NMS
    dets = np.hstack((boxes, scores[:, np.newaxis])).astype(np.float32, copy=False)
    keep = py_cpu_nms(dets, self.nms_threshold)
    # keep = nms(dets, args.nms_threshold,force_cpu=args.cpu)
    dets = dets[keep, :]
    # landms = landms[keep]

    # keep top-K faster NMS
    dets = dets[:self.topK, :]
    # landms = landms[:args.keep_top_k, :]

    # dets = np.concatenate((dets, landms), axis=1)
    # print('post processing time: {:.4f}s'.format(time.time() - tic))

    boxes2D = []
    if len(dets): 
        for face in dets:
            # fractional pixel coordinates -> round? int()? I will loose precision if I do it but drawing does not work and cropping might not work as well
            boxes2D.append(Box2D((int(face[0]), int(face[1]), int(face[2]), int(face[3])), face[4], 'Face'))
    if self.draw:
        image = self.drawer(image, boxes2D)
    return {'image': image, 'boxes2D': boxes2D}

def SHAPE_PREDICTOR_68_FACE_LANDMARKS():
    """Return the path to dlib's 68 face landmark shape predictor, downloading it if necessary.

    The compressed model is downloaded from the dlib-models repository to ``src/models``,
    decompressed, and the archive is removed.

    Returns:
        pathlib.Path: Path to ``shape_predictor_68_face_landmarks.dat``.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the file is missing after decompression, e.g. because it was
            deleted externally.
    """
    predictor_path = Path(__file__).absolute().parent.parent / "models" / \
        'shape_predictor_68_face_landmarks.dat'
    compressed_file = Path(predictor_path.parent /
                           (predictor_path.name + '.bz2'))
    if not predictor_path.exists():
        download_url('https://github.com/davisking/dlib-models/raw/master/shape_predictor_68_face_landmarks.dat.bz2',
                     compressed_file)

        with open(predictor_path, 'wb') as new_file, bz2.BZ2File(compressed_file, 'rb') as file:
            for data in iter(lambda: file.read(100 * 1024), b''):
                new_file.write(data)

        # remove compressed file
        compressed_file.unlink()

        if predictor_path.exists():
            return predictor_path
        else:  # This case should never happen! is only possible if file is deleted externally
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                errno.ENOENT, os.strerror(errno.ENOENT), predictor_path)
    else:
        return predictor_path

def predict_with_nones(x, model, preprocess=None, postprocess=None):
    """Preprocess, predict and postprocess a batch that may contain None.

    If the batch (after preprocessing) is None, the output is None. If it contains None
    entries, the output contains None at the same positions. Postprocessing is skipped when the
    batch is None, empty, or contains only None entries.

    Args:
        x: Input batch for the model; may be None or contain None.
        model: Callable, e.g. a Keras model.
        preprocess: Callable used to preprocess ``x``.
        postprocess: Callable used to postprocess the output of the model.

    Returns:
        The (postprocessed) model output for the batch with None at the positions of None inputs,
        None if the batch is None, or an empty list for an empty batch. A ``tf.Tensor`` output
        is converted to a numpy array.
    """
    if preprocess is not None:
        x = preprocess(x)
    if x is None:
        return None # this skips post processing
    if len(x) == 0:
        return [] # this skips post processing
    elif any(sample is None for sample in x):
        # create mapping and remove Nones from the batch
        non_none_pairs = [(i, val) for i, val in enumerate(x) if val is not None and val is not [] is not None]   
        if non_none_pairs:
            indices, non_nones = zip(*non_none_pairs)     
            # apply model
            inference = model(np.array(non_nones))
            # apply mapping to recreate batch with Nones
            y = [None] * len(x)
            for idx, val in zip(indices, inference):
                y[idx] = val
        else: # if the input only contains Nones
            return x # this skips post processing
    else:
        y = model(np.array(x))
    if isinstance(y, tf.Tensor):
        y = y.numpy()
    if postprocess is not None:
        y = postprocess(y)
    return y

def __init__(self, cfg, format:str="tensor", image_size=None, phase='train'):
    """Compute the feature map sizes for the given configuration and image size.

    Args:
        cfg: RetinaFace configuration, e.g. ``cfg_re50``. Uses the keys 'min_sizes', 'steps'
            and 'clip'.
        format: Kept for compatibility with the original code; the output is always numpy.
        image_size: ``(height, width)`` of the network input.
        phase: Unused; kept for compatibility with the original code.
    """
    super(PriorBox, self).__init__()
    self.min_sizes = cfg['min_sizes']
    self.steps = cfg['steps']
    self.clip = cfg['clip']
    self.image_size = image_size
    self.feature_maps = [[ceil(self.image_size[0]/step), ceil(self.image_size[1]/step)] for step in self.steps]
    self.name = "s"
    self.__format = format

def forward(self):
    """Generate the prior boxes.

    Returns:
        numpy.ndarray: Array of shape ``(num_priors, 4)`` with priors in center-offset form
        ``(cx, cy, w, h)``, normalized to the image size.
    """
    anchors = []
    for k, f in enumerate(self.feature_maps):
        min_sizes = self.min_sizes[k]
        for i, j in product(range(f[0]), range(f[1])):
            for min_size in min_sizes:
                s_kx = min_size / self.image_size[1]
                s_ky = min_size / self.image_size[0]
                dense_cx = [x * self.steps[k] / self.image_size[1] for x in [j + 0.5]]
                dense_cy = [y * self.steps[k] / self.image_size[0] for y in [i + 0.5]]
                for cy, cx in product(dense_cy, dense_cx):
                    anchors += [cx, cy, s_kx, s_ky]

    # back to torch land
    # if self.__format == "tensor":
    #     output = torch.Tensor(anchors).view(-1, 4)
    # elif self.__format == "numpy":
    output = np.array(anchors).reshape(-1, 4)
    # else:
    #     print(TypeError(("ERROR: INVALID TYPE OF FORMAT")))

    if self.clip:
        # if self.__format == "tensor":
        #     output.clamp_(max=1, min=0)
        # else:
        output = np.clip(output, 0, 1)

    return output

def py_cpu_nms(dets, thresh):
    """Apply non-maximum suppression (pure numpy baseline).

    Args:
        dets: Detections of shape ``(N, 5)`` as ``(x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max, score)``.
        thresh: IoU threshold above which the lower-scoring box is suppressed.

    Returns:
        list: Indices into ``dets`` of the kept detections, in descending score order.
    """
    x1 = dets[:, 0]
    y1 = dets[:, 1]
    x2 = dets[:, 2]
    y2 = dets[:, 3]
    scores = dets[:, 4]

    areas = (x2 - x1 + 1) * (y2 - y1 + 1)
    order = scores.argsort()[::-1]

    keep = []
    while order.size > 0:
        i = order[0]
        keep.append(i)
        xx1 = np.maximum(x1[i], x1[order[1:]])
        yy1 = np.maximum(y1[i], y1[order[1:]])
        xx2 = np.minimum(x2[i], x2[order[1:]])
        yy2 = np.minimum(y2[i], y2[order[1:]])

        w = np.maximum(0.0, xx2 - xx1 + 1)
        h = np.maximum(0.0, yy2 - yy1 + 1)
        inter = w * h
        ovr = inter / (areas[i] + areas[order[1:]] - inter)

        inds = np.where(ovr <= thresh)[0]
        order = order[inds + 1]

    return keep
